terms.text: Many simple trend tests vote, from −1 (all down) to +1 (all up); a clear majority up = up-trend, a clear majority down = down-trend. Stocks must also beat the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100: the check closest to 0 counts (0 if they point opposite ways).
Short-term overbought and oversold gauges, averaged: −1 very scared to +1 very greedy. Upper half = overbought, lower half = oversold. Always on the stock’s own chart.
The trend is judged only on a calm day (mood crosses 0) and held until the next: the ring. The rope runs to today's trend. A long rope to the left on a candidate is the author's warning.
High timing in an up-trend = good timing. SPY (calm-day trend +0.35) gets there once its mood drops below −0.65 (now −0.59); a mood above 0 must first cross 0, which re-judges the trend.

rules.means: up-trend on a scared day: high timing
today clearly up, the calm day not yet
calm-day trend not clearly up or down
down-trend on a greedy day: very low timing
